text:
alex: heads up — after the authz prefilter cut yesterday we're seeing dashboard 95p latency jump ~120ms on read-heavy tenants. noticed it in the dash SLI dashboard :chart_with_upwards_trend:

morgan: ugh. same spike in prod trace sampling. looks like the prefilter lookups are causing extra fanout on long queries

sam: can you paste an example span? is it the token validation or the resource lookup that's hot

alex: here — simplified trace: 
```
query->preflight-authz(service=authz-sidecar)->fanout(10)->db
```
we added an extra sidecar hop per sub-query (per panel) instead of pushing prefilter upstream. that multiplies auth calls

jen: right — the old model did a single auth check at gateway level and passed down a filtered statement. new model is fine-grained but multiplies latency

taylor: tradeoff summary: 
- prefilter at gateway: lower fanout, simpler caching, coarser perms (risk of overfiltering)
- inline authz: precise per-row permissions, higher call volume, more tail latency
- sidecar async: accept slightly stale auth decisions with cache TTL

morgan: objective: keep 99p < 300ms for dashboard panel renders. current 99p jumped to ~420ms for heavy dashboards

sam: options I see: 
1) immediate rollback to gateway-prefilter for panels (fast fix)
2) add a batched authz API that accepts multiple resources per call (medium work)
3) local KV cache in sidecar with per-tenant warming + LRU (fast-medium)
4) async-degrade: return partial panel results while auth verifies in background (UX tradeoff)

alex: +1 to (2) and (3). batching would be ideal long-term to keep correctness and reduce RPCs. KV cache plus smart warmup could mitigate now

jen: caution on cache: eviction patterns for large tenants will still cause tail spikes. need tenant-aware rate limits and a slow-path circuit

taylor: also consider a hybrid: gateway prefilter for common queries (top 20 panel types), and inline/batched authz for the rest. reduces overall volume while keeping granularity

morgan: for rollout: canary 5% of tenants with batching and cache enabled, measure 95p/99p and auth error rate. also verify no new permission regressions via unit evals

sam: prototype for batched API: 
```
POST /authz/batch 
{ tenant_id, resources: [ {type, id}, ... ], action: "view" }
```
returns map resource->allow/deny

alex: infra-bot did a quick deploy: 
infra-bot: deploy finished: authz-sidecar v2.3 -> prod (canary=5%) :rocket:

jen: action items: 
- sam: spike batched authz (API + server) (ETA 2w)
- taylor: KV cache design doc, include tenant warming & eviction policy (ETA 5d)
- morgan: set up canary metrics, 95p/99p panels + auth error alerts (ETA 2d)
- alex: coordinate temporary gateway-prefilter toggle for worst offenders (ETA today)

alex: also add a debug trace flag to correlate panel->auth calls so we can attribute tail latency to auth vs DB

taylor: note re: security: any prefilter must be conservative — prefer allow-listing only when fully confident. document fallback behaviour

sam: quick perf note — batching reduces RPC overhead but you still pay for RBAC evaluation CPU. add a microcache for decision TTL 30s to smooth spikes

morgan: ok, sounds like a plan. I'll own the canary dashboard and post results in this thread in 48h

infra-bot: alert: canary=5% baseline metrics captured. authz 95p latency: 210ms, dashboard panel 95p: 310ms (pre-change was 190ms)

alex: thanks — loop back after metrics. if 95p stays >350ms we rollback gateway toggle and prioritize batching

jen: one last thing — add a regression test in the eval harness that runs a synthetic heavy dashboard (10 panels, multi-tenant) to catch future perf regressions

taylor: will add test vectors and a doc section for operational playbook (how to flip gateway-prefilter + identify tenants)

morgan: I'll post the canary dashboard link when green. cheers :thumbsup:
